label: Scene 3D
tagline: The shared WebGL render layer - splits a 3D scene per subsystem (each rendered standalone) and emits a drivable scene
description: The SHARED 3D render orchestrator - symmetric to visual-orchestrator but for WebGL scenes. Builds ONE drivable three.js scene (one sceneId) by fanning the render work out into PARALLEL SUBSYSTEM teams: research is a single tech pass that ALSO emits a subsystems[] decomposition (one entry per heavy effect - hero object / grass / water / cloth / particle field / volumetric light), the orchestrator scaffolds one s3d_subsystem_ node per entry (N=1 for a one-object hero → degenerate), each subsystem owns its own {geometry+material+sim} and MUST paint a real frame STANDALONE before composition, then s3d-runtime-composer assembles them under one shared renderer/env/post-chain and exposes the drivable scene API window.__scene3d (self-driven rAF OR host-driven step()). Generalises + replaces the four bespoke 3D builders (h3d-scene-author / sim-3d-scene-builder / game-world-builder / im-output-3d). Used directly for the hero slot AND linked by simulation / narrative / game / interactive-media / motion-studio for their heavy-3D render (mode=host-driven, the caller's loop drives the handles). The plain `3d` drawer remains the right cost for a simple single-object slot; this is the escalation for Spline-grade material quality and/or multi-subsystem scenes.

triggers.title: 3d-hero slot escalation (through the hero-3d alias)
triggers.rule: visual-orchestrator classifies a slot as `3d-hero`; the parent dispatches hero-3d-orchestrator, now a thin alias that translates the hero envelope to a scene-3d brief (mode=self-driven) and co-dispatches this orchestrator.

triggers.title: Heavy-3D render for a sim / narrative / game / interactive-media / motion-studio piece
triggers.rule: When an experience orchestrator commits a `3d-environment` paradigm (or a 3d output medium / a real-time 3D scene), it does NOT hand-build the 3D world - it co-dispatches scene-3d-orchestrator with mode=host-driven and drivenHandles = the entities its loop/physics/spine/mapping moves, then drives the scene each frame via window.__scene3d.step(state, alpha).
triggers.ruleSource: simulation / narrative / game / interactive-media / motion-studio orchestrator specs - '3d-environment → render via the shared layer'

triggers.title: Explicit Spline-grade / multi-subsystem scene request
triggers.rule: User explicitly asks for a Spline-grade / cinematic / physically-lit 3D scene, or one with several heavy GPU subsystems (glass + grass + water + cloth + particles). Chat dispatches scene-3d-orchestrator directly with the §1 envelope; after hand-off, chat drives the build per simulation-orchestrator.md §5.1.0 shape.
